note: SPOILERS. Text for the hidden things.

rows.text: At the foot of the dead tree there is a very small door, locked, with a very small doormat. Wipe your feet, it suggests.
A canoe with a hole in it. A name is painted on the bow, crossed out, and a better name painted underneath: STILL FLOATS (MOSTLY).
Under the lean-to, a biscuit tin of supplies, and a note: Take what you need. Leave something for the next ranger.
One large, slow ripple crosses the pond from one side to the other. Then nothing. The water is perfectly still.
A survey stake with a faded ribbon. Someone has written on it: TOWER, THIS WAY. KEEP GOING. The writing gets less tidy the further you go.
Seven ordinary mushrooms in a perfect circle. Just mushrooms. Probably.
A boulder shaped very much like a sleeping bear. Very much. It might be snoring.
Carved in the bark: RANGER WAS HERE. And under it, in a different hand: SO WAS I.
The lookout's tally book. Smokes spotted: 0. Lights spotted: 214.
Day one. The tower radio works if you thump it. It's a good radio, if a little ahead of itself. Weather tomorrow: fine, it says. I'll let you know. - R.
A mossy stone bench, facing a blank rock wall, as if there were a view. It's quite a nice wall.
An old park truck, rusted solid, with a tree growing up through the bonnet. The keys are still in it.
BRIDGE TOLLS, says the board. Every price has been scratched out. Small pawprints in the mud lead out onto the bridge and stop at the gap.
A tunnel through the blackberry thicket, far too low for a person, worn smooth by something.
